title: [observability] the Core lines restores read a drill unit only the user manager knows from the user manager, so the controllers' --user drill is not counted as never passed
prompt:
Spawn, objective 231 [observability] (the lead's ask of 2026-11-19 11:11 from rev-k's survey 10:42; scope YES 12:05 with one condition; author rev-i; readers rev-j first, rev-k second; R2 answers rev-j's two R1 candidates before his run and rev-k's R1 F1): the Core lines restores read a drill unit that only the user manager knows from the user manager, so the controllers' drill, a --user unit that passes daily, is not counted as never passed.

Base: live main 7d5bc8bd.

The problem. serve/core_lines/drills.rs reads a restores row's `unit` with `systemctl show -p Result,ExecMainStatus,ExecMainExitTimestamp --timestamp=unix -- <unit>`: the system manager. spawn-backup-restore-drill-controllers.service is a --user unit (deploy/backup/README.md installs it in ~/.config/systemd/user, and its row in the Core lines file is a plain "unit", as the README says). For a unit it does not know, the system manager answers LoadState=not-found, Result=success, ExecMainStatus=0 and an empty ExecMainExitTimestamp, which reads as no pass and no last run. On live at 12:0x, `systemctl --user show` gave Result=success, ExecMainStatus=0, ExecMainExitTimestamp=@1795039661 (06:07 that morning), and /api/core-lines said the Controllers row had never passed: "restores passed in 7 days: 3 of 6", one short.

What changes (crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/drills.rs):
- show() asks for LoadState as well, and takes `user`: `--user` before `show` when it is set.
- A unit row's reading (read_unit): the system manager's answer as before. When that answer says LoadState=not-found, the unit is asked once of the user manager (`--user show ...`), with the same bound (UNIT_LIMIT), a log line for each call, and the same 60 s keep. Its Result, ExecMainStatus and exit timestamp give the pass and the last run as for a system unit.
- A unit known to both managers is read from the system manager only. An answer with no LoadState line (a stand-in, an older systemd) is the system manager's and is never asked again.
- The module doc and show()'s doc say this.

What stays as it is: the record rows; the unit name check (unit_allowed); the bound, the keep, the log's form; parse_show and parse_last; the north star's rule; the Core lines file (no config key, no owner edit of ws/core-lines.json: the live Controllers row starts reading at the deploy). Cost: one more systemctl call per user-unit row per minute (the keep), 1-2 ms timed on live; no database read.

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/drills.rs (with its unit tests). Owner: rsi/scenarios/231.sh, rsi/backlog/231.json.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/231.sh, black box. A real `spawn serve` on its own database reads GET /api/core-lines with a stand-in SPAWN_SYSTEMCTL that answers as the system manager, or as the user manager when its first argument is --user. Each call is logged, and the stand-in prints only the properties -p names, as systemctl does.
- (1) usr-c (only the user manager knows it, passed 10 h ago) has its passed_at_ms and last from the --user answer. usr-f (user only, failed) has no pass and last {ok false, "Result=exit-code, ExecMainStatus=1"}.
- (2) none-x, known to neither, has no pass and no last.
- (3) sys-a, known to both managers (the lead's condition; the user manager would give another time), and legacy-l (an answer with no LoadState) keep the system manager's answer. --user is asked exactly for usr-c, usr-f and none-x, once each. (3k, rev-k's R1 F1) sys-f (a system unit that failed; the user manager would say passed) keeps its failure, and sys-e (its system call exits 1) has no reading: neither is asked of the user manager.
- (4) restores_passed counts usr-c: 4 (sys-a, legacy-l, masked-m, usr-c), where the system manager alone gives 3.
- (5) a second reading within 60 s asks systemctl nothing more.
- (6) only LoadState=not-found falls back: masked-m (LoadState=masked, passed 10 h ago; the user manager would say another time) keeps the system answer and is never asked with --user. The serve's log says each user call ("core-lines: <systemctl> show usr-c.service: not a system unit (N ms); asking the user manager", then "core-lines: <systemctl> --user show usr-c.service: N ms"), and has no --user line for sys-a.
On live main 7d5bc8bd, 231.sh exits 1 at (1). 093.sh, 105.sh and 112.sh (the other SPAWN_SYSTEMCTL scenarios) still pass.

Tests (unit, drills.rs): a unit the system manager does not know is read from the user manager (both calls' argv); a failed user unit says its result; a system unit, failed or passed or with no LoadState line, is never asked of the user manager; a unit neither knows has no pass; a system call that fails is not asked of the user manager; not_found reads only LoadState, and no other load state (masked, error, bad-setting, merged, stub) is not-found. The argv test's expected -p gains LoadState. No test is renamed or dropped.

Verified by: after landing and the deploy, /api/core-lines's Controllers row has passed_at_ms at the drill's last 06:0x run, and restores_passed counts it. A serve log line "systemctl --user show spawn-backup-restore-drill-controllers.service: N ms" shows the call (the lead reads both).
